newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Nizhny Novgorod region says rated by Moody's, S&P.
newsitem.headline: Nizhny Novgorod region says rated by Moody's, S&P.

text.p: An official from Russia's Nizhny Novgorod region said on Tuesday that Moody's and Standard & Poor's had assigned its planned Eurobond high speculative ratings.
Moody's has assigned Nizhny Novgorod Ba2 and Standard & Poor's BB-, Andrei Zotikov, deputy chief executive of the regional agency for aid to investment, told Reuters by telephone.
The ratings are the same as those assigned to Russia for its sovereign Eurobond by the two agencies last year.
Zotikov said the region was ready to issue the bond, whose volume would not exceed $100 million, but was waiting for a government regulation on regional Eurobond issues to be issued.
The Russian government is drawing up regulations for regions issuing Eurobonds, which will also cover taxation of such paper.
Last week, the government agreed in principle not to subject regional Eurobonds to a new 15-percent tax on earnings from government securities earnings.
Zotikov said Nizhny Novgorod region would issue the five-year Eurobond in April or May.
On Monday, the City of Moscow received the same ratings as Russia and Nizhny Novgorod and plans to issue a Eurobond soon.
Russia itself plans to issue a second Eurobond, denominated in marks, in March.
But Zotikov said he was not discouraged by competition from other Russian borrowers.
"Demand will be quite high, no matter whether Moscow comes in before us or not," he said.
